title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
technique: prefill/decode disaggregation onto separate GPUs with per-phase parallelism and replica counts chosen by a simulator-driven goodput-maximizing placement algorithm, bandwidth-aware placement

optimized_metrics.evidence: an effective LLM serving system should balance these needs and maximize per-GPU goodput, defined as the maximum request rate that can be served adhering to the SLO attainment goal (say, 90%) for each GPU provisioned
Given the application's TTFT and TPOT requirements, DistServe co-optimizes the resource allocation and parallelism strategy tailored for each phase.
DistServe ... staying within latency constraints for > 90% of requests

headline_claim.text: DistServe can serve 7.4x more requests or 12.6x tighter SLO, compared to state-of-the-art systems, while staying within latency constraints for > 90% of requests.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 8-9 (vs per-GPU rate and SLO scale; 90% and 99% targets)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the time to first token (TTFT), which is the duration of the prefill phase
metric_definitions.notes: informally prefill duration, but footnote/§2.2 says latency comprises execution time plus queuing delay (the TTFT model Eq.1 includes queuing); SLO attainment is measured on request-level TTFT incl. queuing

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the time per output token (TPOT), which represents the average time taken to generate a token for each request (except for the first token)
metric_definitions.notes: per-request average, excludes first token; footnote 1: 'The overall request latency equals TTFT plus TPOT times the number of generated tokens.'

metric_definitions.definition_quote: per-GPU goodput, defined as the maximum request rate that can be served adhering to the SLO attainment goal (say, 90%) for each GPU provisioned
metric_definitions.notes: request-rate goodput, normalized per GPU provisioned; SLO = both TTFT and TPOT must be met per request

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SLO attainment (the proportion of requests that meet the SLOs)
ments in Table 1 simultaneously using a parameter called SLO Scale. As SLO Scale decreases, the latency requirement becomes more stringent.
metric_definitions.notes: multiplier on both TTFT and TPOT SLOs used to find tightest SLO met at 90%

slo_spec: Table 1, set empirically ('there exists no available SLO settings'): chatbot OPT-13B TTFT 0.25s / TPOT 0.1s; OPT-66B 2.5s/0.15s; OPT-175B 4.0s/0.2s; code completion OPT-66B 0.125s/0.2s; summarization OPT-66B 15s/0.15s; attainment goal 90% (99% in appendix)
load_regime: request-rate sweep with Poisson arrivals over datasets without timestamps; SLO-scale sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: chunked prefill 'trades TTFT for TPOT and cannot eliminate the interference'; disaggregation adds KV transfer overhead (found <0.1% of latency)
hardware: 4 nodes x 8 NVIDIA A100-80GB (NVLink; 25 Gbps cross-node)
workloads: ShareGPT (chatbot), HumanEval (code completion), LongBench (summarization); Poisson arrivals
extractor_notes: Goodput here is request-rate at 90% joint TTFT+TPOT attainment, per GPU (cost proxy). Fig 1 motivation reports P90 TTFT/TPOT while the system itself optimizes attainment. Baselines vLLM and DeepSpeed-MII.
load_class_quote: request-rate sweep with Poisson arrivals over datasets without timestamps; SLO-scale sweep (§6)
repass_log: all entries already design (goodput goal, TTFT/TPOT SLO constraints)
